text:
maria: ran a quick weight-only INT8 bakeoff on aurora-13b (tokenizer v2). comparing bitsandbytes (bnb) and llm.int8 (llmint8). pasting notes + raw eval bot summary so folks can skim.

maria: full command I used (single-node A100-80GB):
```
python tools/quant_eval.py \\n  --model ckpts/aurora-13b-v1 \\n  --quant bnb,llmint8 \\n  --mode weight-only \\n  --batch 8 \\n  --max-len 512 \\n  --slices mmlu,hellaswag,lambada,math-synthetic,chat-safety \\n  --output /tmp/aurora13b-int8-bake.json
```

maria: earlier runs used p50/p95 latency capture and peak GPU mem. seeded runs with seed=42, single-shot eval for MMLU/HellaSwag; LAMBADA used full-auto perplexity.

eval-bot: SUMMARY AUTO-EVAL: aurora-13b | weight-only INT8 | bnb vs float32, llmint8 vs float32

- bnb (w-INT8 default): MMLU -1.9% abs, HellaSwag -3.4% abs, LAMBADA ppl +11.7%, math-synthetic accuracy -4.5% abs, chat-safety FP rate +0.6%
- llmint8 (w-INT8): MMLU -1.2% abs, HellaSwag -2.1% abs, LAMBADA ppl +5.8%, math-synthetic -1.1% abs, chat-safety +0.1%

- perf bnb: peak GPU 37.8GB, p50 76ms, p95 205ms
- perf llmint8: peak GPU 41.9GB, p50 94ms, p95 248ms

maria: first pass takeaway: llmint8 slightly better quality across most slices but higher mem and slower tail latency. bnb is faster but shows outsized hit on long-context LAMBADA and synthetic math.

kai: LAMBADA and math regressions point to numeric stability in attention / accumulation. did you try bnb grouping/clipping params? sometimes 8bit_grouping or threshold fixes attention drift.

maria: re-ran bnb with 8bit_grouping=128 and 8bit_threshold=0.01 (config flags) and re-collected. quick diff below.

eval-bot: PATCH RUN: bnb(group128)
- bnb(group128): MMLU -1.5% abs, HellaSwag -2.6% abs, LAMBADA ppl +5.2%, math-synthetic -2.3% abs, chat-safety +0.3%
- perf bnb(group128): peak GPU ~38.9GB, p50 82ms, p95 218ms

sylvia: grouping makes a big dent on LAMBADA (good) but math slice still shows stepwise errors. could be rounding accumulation in FFN or softmax normalization numeric range. we should diff activations per layer on failed examples.

devon: @maria can you paste one concrete LAMBADA failure and one math failure (gold / float / bnb) so we can inspect? also include model run flags (kv-cache on/off).

maria: sample LAMBADA fail (shortened):
- GOLD: "He warned that the bridge would close at dusk"
- FLOAT32: "the bridge would close at dusk"
- BNB: "the bridge would open at dawn"

maria: math failure example: two-step add problem (shortened):
- GOLD: "42"
- FLOAT32: "42"
- BNB: "43"  (off by one)

kai: that off-by-one smells like precision loss in an incremental aggregation; FFN clamp or GELU approximation could be the culprit. try per-layer max/min activation histograms vs float.

sylvia: also test disabling kv-cache for LAMBADA to see if past-key quant noise compounds. kv-cache was enabled on these runs.

maria: quick experiments:
- bnb(group128) + kv-cache disabled -> LAMBADA ppl +4.8% (slightly better), p50 increased ~8ms
- llmint8 with fused-gemm + kv-cache enabled -> same quality as before, p50 unchanged

maria: operational suggestion for routing / prod profile:
- default low-latency route: bnb weight-only with grouping=128, kv-cache enabled
- critical eval/safety endpoints: llmint8 or float32 pinned (higher mem/latency but better quality)
- auto-fallback: if post-deploy evals detect >2% abs drop on any safety/eps-critical slice or p95 > 400ms, route traffic to float32 pool and alert 

devon: do we have slice-level guardrails? current monitors are coarse. we should add slice thresholds + an auto-abort/rollback hook in the rollout pipeline. filing ticket: TICKET-2456 to add slice-level abort rules and daily calibrations.

maria: added results JSON to datasets/quant-sweeps (local path) and will open PR with README describing grouping param impact and the runtime flags used.

kai: two asks: 1) run a per-layer activation delta job for the two failing LAMBADA examples (float vs bnb) to pinpoint where distributions diverge; 2) try a tiny GPTQ-style fast calibrate on top of bnb weights (act-order or bias-correction) to see if math slice corrects.

sylvia: note for oncall: when we flip a model to bnb(group128) profile, add a canary step that runs math-synthetic + LAMBADA slices on the canary traffic before full rollout.

maria: will queue the activation-diff job and the small calibrate experiment. will report back in-thread with per-layer plots and updated numbers. TL;DR: for aurora-13b weight-only INT8, bnb + grouping is the best latency/quality trade after tuning; llmint8 is more plug-and-play for quality but costs more. LAMBADA (long-context) and math-synthetic are the most sensitive slices.

kai: thanks, good writeup.

sylvia: :+1:

devon: tagging this for the model-onboarding checklist and follow-ups.
